title: For True Peace, Ceasefires Must Address Digital Warfare Too
Launch of the Digital Ceasefire and De-escalation Handbook at the Paris Peace Forum
body_markdown:
The Human Rights Center at UC Berkeley School of Law will officially launch the **Digital Ceasefire and De-escalation Handbook (DCDH)** at the **2026 Paris Peace Forum** on 10 November.

Developed by Brett Solomon and Betsy Popken, the Handbook provides a practical framework for mediators, negotiating parties, and affected communities to address harmful digital operations during armed conflict, grey-zone activity, and internal disturbance. It offers guidance for negotiating commitments to constrain internet interference, information threats, and cyber attacks, helping to protect civilians, reduce hostilities, and build pathways towards Digital Peace.

The launch will feature an interactive simulation, **"Negotiating Peace in a Digital World: An Interactive Simulation on Digital Ceasefire."** Participants will take on the roles of opposing parties negotiating a fragile ceasefire, using the Handbook to develop provisions addressing digital hostilities. An unexpected digital crisis will then put their agreements to the test, demonstrating the challenges and opportunities of integrating digital de-escalation into contemporary peace processes.

**Event details**

- **Date:** Tuesday, 10 November 2026
- **Time:** 16:15–17:00
- **Location:** Stage C, Musée de l'Homme, Paris
- **Speakers:** Betsy Popken, Executive Director, Human Rights Center at UC Berkeley School of Law, and Brett Solomon, Senior Research Fellow, Human Rights Center at UC Berkeley School of Law.

The launch marks an important milestone in advancing the integration of digital ceasefire and de-escalation provisions into peace negotiations and conflict resolution efforts worldwide.

The Digital Ceasefire & De-escalation Platform is now live. You can [read the Handbook](#/handbook) section by section, or [build your own Agreement](#/builder) from its model provisions and download it as Word, Markdown or PDF. You can also [download the Handbook](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NvCVnaQAGpcAy56_eHXWbdjYUv6CJos933_SeYZulVI/edit?usp=sharing).

The Platform is an initiative of the [Human Rights Center](https://humanrights.berkeley.edu/) at UC Berkeley School of Law.
